title_en: Provisions on Radio Regulation of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Provisions are formulated for the purpose of ensuring the effective implementation of radio control, safeguarding national security and the public interest.

Article 2 For the purpose of these Provisions, "radio control" means the compulsory management of the emission, radiation and propagation of radio waves by, according to law, taking measures such as restricting or prohibiting the use of radio stations, radio transmitting equipment and non-radio equipment that radiates radio waves, and implementing technical blocking of specific radio frequencies, within a specific time period and a specific area.

Article 3 The state may implement radio control as needed for safeguarding national security, ensuring major state missions, handling major emergencies, or other such needs.
Radio control implemented within the whole country or across provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government shall be decided by the State Council and the Central Military Commission.
Radio control implemented within a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall be decided by the people's government of that province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government and the relevant military command, and shall be reported to the State Council and the Central Military Commission for recordation.

Article 4 Implementation of radio control shall follow the principles of scientific planning and reasonable implementation, minimizing the impact of radio control on the national economy and the production and daily life of the people.

Article 5 The state radio regulatory authority and the military electromagnetic spectrum management authority shall, based on the needs of radio control and in conjunction with relevant departments of the State Council, formulate nationwide radio control plans, which shall be submitted to the State Council and the Central Military Commission for approval.
The radio regulatory authority of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government and the electromagnetic spectrum management authority of a military command shall, based on the nationwide radio control plans and in conjunction with relevant departments of the people's government of that province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, formulate radio control plans for that region, which shall be submitted to the people's government of that province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government and the military command for approval.

Article 6 The organ that decides to implement radio control shall issue a radio control order 10 days before the radio control begins, specifying the area, subject, start and end time, frequency range, and other relevant requirements of the radio control, except in emergencies requiring immediate implementation of radio control.

Article 7 Where the State Council and the Central Military Commission decide to implement radio control within the whole country or across provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, the state radio regulatory authority and the military electromagnetic spectrum management authority shall, in conjunction with the Ministry of Public Security and other relevant departments of the State Council, form a radio control coordination body responsible for the organization and coordination of the radio control.
Where radio control is implemented within a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, the radio regulatory authority of that province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government and the electromagnetic spectrum management authority of the military command shall, in conjunction with the public security department and other relevant departments, form a radio control coordination body responsible for the organization and coordination of the radio control.

Article 9 During the implementation of radio control, units or individuals that own, use, or manage radio stations, radio transmitting equipment, or non-radio equipment that radiates radio waves within the radio control area shall comply with the radio control order and radio control instructions.

Article 10 During the implementation of radio control, the relevant local people's governments, departments and units of transportation, railways, radio and television, meteorology, fisheries, communications, electric power, and other sectors, and relevant units of the armed forces and the armed police forces shall assist the state radio regulatory authority and the military electromagnetic spectrum management authority or the radio regulatory authority of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government and the electromagnetic spectrum management authority of the military command in implementing the radio control.

Article 11 When radio control ends, the organ that decided to implement it shall promptly issue a notice of the end of radio control; if the radio control order has already specified the termination time of the radio control, the notice of the end of radio control may be omitted.

Article 12 Any person who violates a radio control order or radio control instructions shall be ordered to make corrections by the state radio regulatory authority or the radio regulatory authority of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government; if the person refuses to make corrections, the relevant equipment may be closed, sealed up, temporarily detained, or dismantled; if the circumstances are serious, the radio station license and radio frequency use permit shall be revoked; if the violation of public security administration provisions occurs, a penalty shall be imposed by the public security organ according to law.
If a relevant unit of the armed forces or the armed police forces violates a radio control order or radio control instructions, the military electromagnetic spectrum management authority or the electromagnetic spectrum management authority of the military command shall order it to make corrections; if the circumstances are serious, the directly responsible persons in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Central Military Commission.
Article 13 These Provisions shall come into force as of November 1, 2010.
